task.title: Syncing with a teammate
task.description: You are in the ~/site folder - a clone of the shared repository https://github.com/team/site.git. You have a local commit that has not been pushed yet, and your teammate Aziz has already pushed his commit with a different file. You have an uncommitted change in notes.md. Write the commands one per line: 1) Check the state and try to push the commit with git push - make sure that Git rejects it. 2) Put the uncommitted change aside with git stash and look at the stash list. 3) Choose a way to combine: git config pull.rebase false (or the --no-rebase / --rebase option of git pull) and take your teammate's changes. 4) Push your commits. 5) Bring back the stashed change (git stash pop) and commit it with the message Update notes. 6) Push the commit and check that the working directory is clean. Do not use git push --force.
task.starter_code:
# Write the commands one per line. Lines starting with # are comments.
# You are in the ~/site folder. Your commit is not pushed yet, Aziz has already pushed his,
# and you have an uncommitted change in notes.md.

# 1. Check the state and try to push the commit (the push will be rejected)

# 2. Put the uncommitted change into the stash and check the list

# 3. Choose a way to combine (pull.rebase false or the --no-rebase / --rebase option) and take the changes

# 4. Push your commits

# 5. Bring back the stashed change and commit it with the message Update notes

# 6. Push the commit and make sure the working directory is clean

tests.name: The first git push was rejected (you saw the error)
tests.fail: Start with git push before git pull - make sure that Git rejects the push (fetch first).

tests.name: The change is put aside with git stash
tests.fail: Before git pull, put the change aside: git stash (or git stash push -m "...").

tests.name: The server has the teammate's commit Add styles
tests.fail: Aziz's commit disappeared from the server - do not use git push --force. First git pull, then git push.

tests.name: The server has your commit Add home page
tests.fail: Your local commit did not get to the server: after git pull run git push. Do not run git reset --hard origin/main.

tests.name: The server has the Update notes commit by Anna Karimova
tests.fail: Bring back the change (git stash pop), commit it: git commit -am "Update notes", and push with git push.

tests.name: notes.md on the server has the stashed change
tests.check:
sim.remote("https://github.com/team/site.git").files("main")["notes.md"] === "# Notes
- add contacts page
- add footer
"
tests.fail: The change from the stash must come back with git stash pop, not git stash drop.

tests.name: The local main matches origin/main and the server
tests.check: repo !== null && repo.commit("main") !== null && repo.commit("origin/main") !== null && repo.commit("main").hash === repo.commit("origin/main").hash && repo.commit("main").hash === sim.remote("https://github.com/team/site.git").tip("main")
tests.fail: After the last commit run git push - the branch must not be ahead of origin/main.

tests.name: The stash list is empty
tests.fail: git stash pop brings back the change and removes the entry from the list. git stash list must be empty.

tests.name: The working directory is clean, no merge or rebase is left unfinished
tests.check: repo !== null && repo.branch === "main" && repo.state() === null && repo.status().clean
tests.fail: At the end git status must answer nothing to commit, working tree clean.

tests.name: The teammate's file style.css appeared on your side
tests.fail: Take your teammate's changes: git pull with the chosen way to combine.

tests.name: git push --force is not used
tests.fail: --force overwrites other people's commits on the server. A rejected push is fixed with git pull.

"

tests.fail: Do not rely on specific file names: stash, pull, push, stash pop, commit -am, push.

hints: A push rejected with the hint fetch first is normal: the server has someone else's commit.
git stash puts the change into a "pocket", git stash list shows what is in it.
Without a setting, git pull with diverged branches answers fatal: Need to specify how to reconcile divergent branches. Run git config pull.rebase false or git pull --no-rebase.
After git pull - git push, then git stash pop.
A change in a file that is already tracked: git commit -am "Update notes", then git push.
Check: git status - nothing to commit, working tree clean; git stash list - empty.

questions.question: Git answered the push: ! [rejected] main -> main (fetch first). What does it mean?
options: You have no rights to the repository
The server has commits that you do not have: take them first
questions.explanation: fetch first means "take it first": someone has already pushed commits. You need git pull, then git push again.

questions.question: Match the setting with what git pull does when branches have diverged.
pairs: Moves your commits on top of the received ones (rebase)
Fast-forward only, otherwise refuses with an error
questions.explanation: Without one of these settings (or an option), git pull with diverged branches ends with fatal: Need to specify how to reconcile divergent branches.

questions.question: The branches have diverged, the pull.rebase setting is not set. What will git pull do?
options: Take the commits into origin/main, but stop with fatal: Need to specify how to reconcile divergent branches.
questions.explanation: Since Git 2.33, git pull asks you to choose a way explicitly: merge, rebase or fast-forward only.

questions.question: Which commands take a teammate's changes with diverged branches without an error (the working tree is clean)?
questions.explanation: --no-rebase is a merge, --rebase is a rebase. --ff-only refuses when branches have diverged, and pull without a setting asks you to choose a way.

questions.question: Which command puts uncommitted changes aside so that the working directory becomes clean? Enter the full command.
questions.explanation: git stash (the same as git stash push) puts the changes into a "pocket" and cleans the working directory.

questions.question: How is git stash pop different from git stash apply?
options: pop brings back the changes and removes the entry from the list, apply brings them back and keeps the entry
pop deletes the changes without bringing them back
apply works only with new files
questions.explanation: pop = apply + drop. If a conflict appears during pop, the entry stays in the list.

questions.question: Match the command with the action.
pairs: Copy one commit into the current branch
questions.explanation: Without -u stash does not touch untracked files. cherry-pick creates a copy of a commit with a new hash.

questions.question: The order of GitHub Flow steps:
options: main → commit → merge → pull request → branch
Branch → commits → push → pull request → review → merge → delete the branch
questions.explanation: Work happens in a short branch, and it gets into main only through a pull request after a review.

questions.question: What is true about git rebase main run in the feature/menu branch?
options: The branch commits are moved on top of main
The moved commits get new hashes
A merge commit is always created
You must not do it with a branch that others already use
questions.explanation: rebase rewrites history: new commits with new hashes, without a merge commit. Published branches that others use are not rebased.

questions.question: What is a pull request?
options: The git pull command on the server
A request to merge a branch, where the team discusses and checks the changes before the merge
questions.explanation: A pull request is a page on GitHub: the branch changes, the discussion, the review, the Merge pull request button.

questions.question: Complete the command so that git pull in this repository always does a merge: git config pull.rebase ______
questions.explanation: pull.rebase false means merge, true means rebase.

questions.question: git pull answered: error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: notes.md. What should you do?
options: Put the change aside (git stash) or commit it, then git pull again
questions.explanation: Git protects your uncommitted change. Put it into the stash, take the changes and bring it back with git stash pop.
